text:
The asset is the third most important thing in your lead magnet.

The post is about half of it, the DM is about a quarter, and the resource itself is maybe 15%.

Nobody measured that split, it's my gut from running them.

The asset is still where everyone spends their two weeks.

I tested the same lead magnet resource under different post copy.

Same resource, same link, different copy and a different image on top of it.

The perceived value went up.

Nothing about the resource changed, only what they thought they were getting before they got it.

Your lead magnet didn't flop because the pdf was ass.

It flopped because the post didn't pull comments, and a beautiful resource behind a dead post does literally nothing.

Rewriting the resource is the first thing everyone reaches for and it fixes nothing.

Two problems that look identical in your analytics:

- normal reach, almost no comments: the title or the promise in your copy
- the reach itself died: distribution, and the magnet had nothing to do with it

People mix these up and go rewrite the asset.

40 lead magnet posts on one account, a $300k/month agency's.

The magnets that named a concrete thing pulled around 4% comment rate.

The broad AI one pulled 0.9%.

Same account, same period, so that gap is the title.

Your lead magnet title has to name a thing they can picture receiving.

"How to fix your creative testing" gets nothing.

"Creative testing checklist" gets comments.

Same topic, but one of them is an object that lands in their DMs and the other is a subject line.

3 lead magnets a week for 18 months.

That's a couple hundred of them, and most of the flops blur together at this point.

The pattern never changed, it was almost always the post and almost never the resource.

Same resource would do nothing one week and do fine later with different copy on top.

A magnet on the agency account went from 7,839 redemptions down to 901 across five DMs in six days.

Nothing was wrong with it, it was spent.

Same magnet, same audience, and the redemptions just fall off.

I rest one 8 to 12 weeks now before running it again.

Comment rate is the only number worth watching on day one, comments divided by views.

Booked calls take weeks, and by then you can't tell which post did it.

Comment rate tells you immediately whether the title and the promise landed.

That's also the part you'd actually go change.

For a quality signal, count how many people who claimed the magnet actually reply to the DM.

Lots of claims and no replies means you pulled the wrong crowd.

That's worse than pulling fewer.

A big claim number looks great in a screenshot and does fuck all for your pipeline.

What happens after the DM goes out:

1. check their profile and decide if they're qualified
2. ask what they thought of the resource
3. ask what they're working on right now

That third one is the qualifying part and it doesn't feel like qualifying.

Don't pitch on the message where you deliver the resource.

You keep the conversation going until they say something that opens the door, usually a problem they bring up themselves.

Then the call comes up and it lands soft, because they said it first.

The freebie version of this stops at the asset. You post it, people comment, they get a link, done, and nobody ever looks at who claimed it.

The step that makes it a machine is a human one, checking who came in and starting a conversation with the ones who are qualified.

Nobody builds that step because it doesn't feel like a system.

A magnet that converts to pipeline has something they have to fill in.

If there's nothing in it they complete themselves, they skim it, close it, and you never hear from them again.

If page three makes them write their own answers, they've done work inside your thing.

The DM after that lands completely differently.

Agency owners build one lead magnet and treat it like a launch.

Two weeks on a really nice pdf, posted once, eleven comments, and then lead magnets don't work.

Mine run 3 a week off the same skill and the same templates, new magnet every time.

The build is the cheap part, running it every week is the whole thing.

Lead magnet posts that ask for a comment or a retweet are getting nerfed on X right now.

Articles are the play there for the moment.

The comment-to-DM version still looks really good on LinkedIn.

So I run the article on X and keep the keyword play on LinkedIn.

If you only have one afternoon for a lead magnet this week, spend all of it on the title and the four lines under it.

Then reuse an asset you already have.

The post is half the result and it's the cheapest part to fix.

Building a new resource is the expensive way to avoid writing a better post.

The honest hole in my own machine: the DM links straight to a Notion page, so there's no landing page and no email capture.

We don't own the contact.

If they never reply, the lead is gone.

I'd rather say that than pretend the chain is finished.
